items_missed: Section 1 (Set Agenda): asked for "about ten minutes" but never gave a real agenda statement (what would be covered) or an explicit "sound good?" confirmation before diving in.

Section 2 (Probe): never got a zip code for the destination address, and skipped garage/storage-unit rooms, hallway/access concerns, whether Karen needed packing help, storage stops, and additional stops.

Section 3 (Pricing): no "pricing is super simple" opener; rattled off what's included (movers, truck, disassembly, no CC fees) without mentioning gas, insurance, wrap pads, or tools; named the On-Time Guarantee but never explained the actual mechanic (miss the window, we start discounting); no full "no hidden fees" list (fuel surcharge, assembly fees).
Section 4 (Clock): never explained when the clock starts (on-site, contract opens) or the 15-minute prorated increments after the 2.5-hour minimum.

Section 5 (Estimate): collected the heavy items (adjustable king bed, credenza, TVs) and the second-floor bedrooms but never tied them back into why the time estimate could move; no equivalents/analogy used, no walk-distance mention.
Section 6 (Save Your Ass): skipped entirely — no prep-before-move-day pitch, no consolidation examples, no "take a carload" tip.
Section 7 (Quote/Booking): never stated office hours or a specific way to reach the branch beyond "give us a callback."
Section 9 (Bonus): covered No Worries Damage Coverage but never mentioned the 60 cents/lb baseline liability coverage.
top_strength: This was a returning customer, and Chauny closed the call having earned unprompted praise: "it's great doing business with you guys again... you guys show up on time. Very nice and professional." She also stayed calm and easy when Karen admitted she'd checked the wrong box on the request form, correcting the move type without any friction.
coaching_note: The Save Your Ass prep speech is completely missing here — that's 10 points every call, and this was a good candidate for it given how many boxes and heavy items (75 boxes, an adjustable king bed, a credenza) are in play. Open with a real agenda statement — what you'll cover, roughly how long, and a "sound good?" — instead of jumping straight into pulling up the form. When you name the On-Time Guarantee, actually explain what it means (we start discounting if we miss the window) instead of just labeling it, and get a zip code on both ends so the address capture is complete.
phone_presence_notes: Polite throughout with a genuinely warm close once Karen volunteered praise, but the info-gathering and pricing stretches lean heavily on repeated filler ("okay, you got it") rather than varied, natural acknowledgment of what she said.
